question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared queue/wake/off notification wake policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical reaction-turn contract, or choose a narrower per-message/per-channel design instead?
rationale: The issue adds user-facing wake/config semantics across multiple channels, and the open PRs implement overlapping API shapes that source inspection cannot choose safely without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Adopt Shared Policy
options.body: Use a shared queue-by-default notification wake policy, then repair or land the best PR candidate with docs, generated config metadata, and channel tests.

options.title: Start Narrow
options.body: Approve a Discord-first or Telegram-first wake contract now, accepting a later unification pass for the other reaction-capable channels.

options.title: Defer Reaction Wakes
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and pause or close the implementation PRs until maintainers want this config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Policy
recommendation.body: Use a shared queue-by-default notification wake policy, then repair or land the best PR candidate with docs, generated config metadata, and channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the active shared-policy PR author and has recent history across the reaction, system-event, and heartbeat wake paths.
